text:
maya: Heads-up — we started seeing a 20-40% tail-latency regression on long-context chat routes after yesterday's batching change. Traces point at KV-store eviction/paging churn + continuous-batcher merges causing head-of-line stalls. :boom:

raj: Ugh. Which change specifically? the merge-on-fill tweak?

maya: Yeah, the change that lets the batcher merge two partial batches if the earlier one is waiting >20ms. It reduces average token latency but seems to amplify worst-case when KV pages are being moved.

tj: Do we have profiler output or flamegraphs?

perf-bot: auto-snapshot uploaded: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/perf/1812345678/kv-pager-flame.html :mag_right:

maya: Quick snippet from the prod rollout logs (filtered):
```
[2026-03-16T14:12:03.452Z] batch_merge: b1=12345 b2=12346 latency=21ms head_lock=true
[2026-03-16T14:12:03.453Z] kvcache: page_eviction start slab=slotpool idx=87 size=2MB
[2026-03-16T14:12:03.488Z] kvcache: page_load finish slab=slotpool idx=92 hit=false
[2026-03-16T14:12:03.490Z] request: waiting_for_kv head_of_line=true
```

pat: Interesting — looks like merge causes a batch with heterogeneous contexts to hold a lock while waiting for a slow page-load for one member. Meanwhile other requests in the merged batch can't progress.

raj: Could be fragmentation + async IO ordering. If slot reuse moves pages around during a merge, we get additional page faults. Any repro on staging?

maya: I put together a small repro harness that simulates long contexts + interleaved short bursts. Run: `./tools/repro_kv_hol --load-profile longcontext.json --batcher merge-20ms`

maya: Short repro logs attached in the artifact: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/repro/1812345678/kvcache-hol-repro.log

tj: Ran it locally. Repro is noisy but visible. Flamegraph shows ~35% CPU in `kv_shard::evict` while waiting in `batch::dispatch` — ordering matches the hypothesis.

raj: Quick mitigation options:
- revert merge-on-fill (safe, loses avg latency wins)
- increase merge timeout to avoid merging across heavy page-moving window
- make batcher respect per-request KV pinning (pin slots for requests that are in-flight)
- early prefetch for long-context requests when they enter queue

pat: Another approach: detect "fragmentation storm" by watching page_fault_rate per-shard and temporarily disable merges for that shard. Cheap and targeted.

maya: I like the shard-level circuit-breaker idea. Lower blast radius. Can we implement a simple rate-threshold today?

tj: Yes — small change in batcher: consult `kvcache.stats(page_faults_last_1s)` before merging. If > X, skip merge for Y ms. I'll prototype.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert created: PR-ops/kv-hol-mitigation-1812345678 -> https://phab/p/PR-7890 :information_source:

raj: Also want to collect a targeted stack trace when we see head_of_line=true with >100ms wait, so we can correlate with slot moves. Add a debug-pointer sample.

maya: I'll add the sampling probe and enable on canary. Plan: tj implements circuit-breaker + probe, we run canary on 10% traffic for 6h, then decide.

pat: If canary looks good, follow-up: design eviction-aware merge algorithm that avoids merging requests that will likely touch different slots (based on k-v key affinity or model prefix). Longer term.

raj: Agreed. For the PR — keep the default off behind the flag. We don't want to hard revert unless metrics demand it.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the canary and post results. :thumbsup:

tj: Working on the patch now, ping me if you want to review test harness.

maya: cc @eng-oncall — FYI in case tail spikes during rollout.

perf-bot: canary started at 1812345800, sample rate=10%

maya: (later) Canary 2h in: tail latency back to baseline on canary, prod still shows 30% regression on affected routes. Looks promising. Will extend to 25% traffic and monitor.

pat: Nice. If we see reversion, we should roll forward the mitigation and schedule the longer-term algorithm.

raj: Thanks all — great troubleshooting cycle.
